title: Lower-Left Probability as an Acceptance Expectation
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a sign-valued Boolean function, and let $a$ be a real coefficient vector on $n$ coordinates. Suppose $f(x)$ is the sign of the linear form with coefficients $a$ for every $x$, and that this linear form is nonzero at every $x$. Under the correlated-pair distribution, the probability that the sum of the pair summands lies in the quadrant with both coordinates nonpositive, converted to a real number, equals the expectation of the indicator that both function values are $-1$.
